review_method: Independent LLM mathematical verification, with exact rational arithmetic corroboration
scope: The exact capacity and retained-volume formulas in Section1 and both counterexamples in Sections2–3.

checks.claim: The complete vertex set and extremal reduction are valid.
checks.reason: The nontrivial cutting plane intersects a supporting simplex face in dimension support-size minus2, so a new vertex has precisely one coordinate from each group. Maximum simplex volume is attained by compactness and can be maximized over each vertex separately; absolute affine determinants attain their maximum at polytope vertices. Thus the finite barycentric determinant calculation is exhaustive.

checks.claim: The determinant upper bound is exact.
checks.reason: Factoring t from each I row,1−t from each J row, and1/t from every pure column leaves a reduced incidence matrix after changing J-row signs. It has N edges on N+1 vertices. A cycle gives a column dependence; an acyclic such graph is connected and hence a tree. Nonroot leaf expansion gives determinant magnitude1. Therefore every simplex ratio is t^(k−p)(1−t)^l times0 or1, and p<=k gives the upper bound(1−t)^l. Taking all k pure vertices and one cut vertex for each J index attains it.

checks.claim: The volume polynomial is correctly normalized.
checks.reason: Grouped uniform barycentric coordinates have beta(k,l) density with normalization d!/[(k−1)!(l−1)!]. Its tail agrees with the displayed binomial polynomial by differentiation and the value at0. The formula includes k=1 and l=1.

checks.claim: The centroid-cut counterexample is exact for all stated odd dimensions.
checks.reason: For d=2m−1 and k=l=m, threshold1/2 is the true centroid level, the retained fraction is1/2 by symmetry, and maximal simplex fraction is2^-m. The d5 discrepancy is423/32768. For m>=4, Bernoulli and the decreasing sequence(2m−1)/2^m give the strict lower bound9/16>1/2 for the equivalent failure inequality.
